Item text and resp mapping extracted from the paper's own raw Google Forms data export (PLOS ONE supp file s001.xlsx, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0323406.s001), which contains literal item wording as column headers plus text/numeric response pairs (verified via its 'Recoded' sheet: Never=0,Rarely/Barely=1,Sometimes=2,Frequently=3,Always=4; shifted +1 to match live IRW resp 1-5). The source survey used inconsistent wording for the second-lowest frequency category across items: 'Barely' for stressor items 1-14, 'Rarely' for items 15-29 and all 19 coping items -- both represent the same ordinal position (resp=2) and are transcribed literally per-item as they appear in the source rather than normalized. Paper (Alkouri et al. 2025) names the instrument the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS; Sheu et al. 1997) but gives no separately quotable participant instructions text, so 'instructions' is left blank rather than fabricated.

Dictionary/table name implies a 16-item Barratt Impulsiveness Scale (0-3), but the source paper (Allen et al. 2025, PeerJ 10.7717/peerj.19057) never describes or even names the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale in its main text or STROBE checklist supplement -- the paper explicitly states 'A subset of participants also completed additional neurocognitive tasks and questionnaires; these data are not described here.' The Barratt measure is confirmed present only via column labels (bi1-bi16, plus BarrattImpuls/BIS_Attn1/BIS_Attn2/BIS_Motor1/BIS_Motor2/BIS_Planning1/BIS_Planning2/Barratt_YN) in the paper's own supplementary raw-data workbook (peerj-13-19057-s001.xlsx, sheet 'questionnaire_scoring', fetched via Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles zip endpoint since the PeerJ direct link 403s). Live bi1-bi16 resp values are 0,1,2 only (confirmed via full value counts, no 3s occur anywhere in the data) -- inconsistent with the standard published BIS-11 (30 items, 4-point 1-4 scale) and with the dictionary's stated '0-3' range. The 6 named subscales (Attn1/2, Motor1/2, Planning1/2) match BIS-11's 6 first-order factors grouped into 3 second-order factors, but no source ties bi1-bi16 to specific items/order from the standard 30-item instrument, and no source discloses the response-option wording for the 3-point scale. Web search found no published 16-item, 3-point BIS variant matching this structure. Item text, item order, and option text cannot be recovered with any confidence from available sources; forcing a mapping from the standard BIS-11 item list would be a guess, not a transcription. Recommend either contacting the authors directly for the instrument text, or leaving this table itemtext-incomplete. Also flag the dictionary Description's '0-3' range as inaccurate against live data (should be 0-2, 3-point).

Paper (Almuqbil et al 2022, PeerJ, PMC9575671) administered the Arabic translation of the EPDS (Ghubash et al 1997 validated version), not the English original. The Arabic translated wording could not be independently sourced/verified, so item_text/option_text in the CSV are the standard English EPDS wording (Cox, Holden & Sagovsky 1987) with reverse-scoring applied per the published EPDS scoring key (items 3,5-10 reverse-scored). Item count (10), resp range (0-3), and per-item N (253) match the live data exactly, so structure is validated; only the surface-language wording is an English stand-in for the Arabic instrument actually shown to participants.
